page.layout: Two printed columns of Greek commentary on the left (Greek text with Greek heading and a Greek paragraph, with small Greek and Latin marginal notes in the left margin); a right-hand Latin column block with marginal letters A–H beside it, a heading CAPUT IIII. and running text, continuing below in full width. Running head at top: ARISTOTELIS. Page number 234 at top left; 1100 (signature-like number) bottom right.

main_text.p: τοῦν ἐχόμενον. τοῦτο δὲ διαφερόμενον, φανερὸν, ὅτι ἐν τούτοις ὅτι τὸ σωματος, εἰς ἂν ἐν τι πέρυκε γινέσθω, χ̄ ταῦτι σωμ. κ. τὸ γίνεται τὸ σωμ.
main_text.head: Κεφάλαιον δ'.
main_text.p: Μία δὲ κίνησις λέγεται πολλαχῶς. ἡ κίνησις

Latin column text continues in the right column beginning "extrema sint duo. Hoc definito patet in his esse continuum, ex quibus aptum est unum quid fieri tactu..." and runs to "CAPUT IIII. Quaestio de motus unitate." followed by "VNus autem motus multis dicitur modis..." and continues through "do tanget, aut unū fiet, vltimū lineæ, ambulationisve? Hærētes igitur erūt..." at the foot.
Latin and Greek marginal notes in the left margin and beside lines are the printed side notes of the commentary.

page.notes: The page is dense: the Greek and the Latin text are only partly legible at this scan resolution; parts of the Greek column and of the right column are marked by uncertainty and are not fully transcribed. Right column heading "CAPVT IIII." and "Quaestio de motus unitate." are printed in capitals and italic. Marginal letters A to H run down the middle column edge. Left margin notes are in Greek and Latin (for example "vt ex Alexandro refert Simplicius, quem vide" and "de interpretes"). The bottom-right number 1100 is a printed page reference.
